title: Use data to find where users struggle
summary: Data shows you what users do and where they give up. Use it alongside research: data tells you where the problem is, and talking to users tells you why.

beginner: Pick the user journey linked to your learning questions, for example signing up, completing an order or submitting a form.
Find out what data already exists: product analytics, support tickets, complaints, reviews, survey comments and operational reports. Ask an analyst or engineer where it lives.
Build a simple funnel: list each step and how many people reach it. Look for the step where the most people drop out.
Split the numbers by groups that might behave differently, such as new and returning users, device type or region.
Read 30 to 50 support tickets or comments for the worst step and note the common themes.
Write down three to five 'data signals' with numbers, and the questions they raise for user research.
intermediate: Build a funnel for the target journey and find the largest drop-off in absolute numbers.
Segment by user type, device and channel to find where the problem is concentrated.
Triangulate with support tickets, reviews and survey text.
Summarise signals with numbers and feed the open questions into research.
experienced: Combine behavioural, qualitative and operational data to size each pain point by users affected and value at stake.
Check data quality and tracking gaps before trusting a pattern; note confidence for each signal.
Look for cohort and trend changes, not just a snapshot, to separate new problems from old ones.
Use the signals to aim research at the highest-value questions and to set baselines for later measurement.

canDelegateTo.task: Build the funnel and segment the data
Explain what is tracked, where the data lives and any gaps
Analyse support tickets and comments for themes

toolExamples.ga4: Use a funnel exploration to see drop-off between each step of the journey, then add a breakdown by device category.
toolExamples.amplitude: Build a funnel chart and click on the worst step to see what people did instead.
toolExamples.mixpanel: Create a funnels report and compare conversion for new and returning users.
toolExamples.power-bi: Combine analytics exports with support ticket counts on one page so you can see both together.
toolExamples.claude: Paste anonymised support ticket text and ask it to group the tickets into themes with a count for each. Remove any personal details first.

definitionOfDone: Funnel or step data for the target journey, with the biggest drop-off identified
Three to five data signals written up with numbers and confidence
Open questions handed to user research
pitfalls: Trusting numbers without checking how they are tracked
Looking at percentages only and missing where most people are actually lost
Treating data as the answer to 'why' rather than 'where'

leaderView.good: Teams use data to find where users struggle, then use research to find out why.
ask: What does the data show about where users drop off?
Which of these signals have we checked with real users?
signs: Decisions rest on a single chart with no context.
Data and research tell different stories, and no one has noticed.
